cards.title: Does P equal NP?
cards.target: Does every language with polynomially bounded, polynomial-time verifiable certificates admit a deterministic polynomial-time decision algorithm? Equivalently, do there exist a deterministic Turing machine A and constants C,k such that, for every encoded Boolean formula F of bit length n, A decides whether F has a satisfying assignment and halts within $C(n+1)^k$ steps? The algorithm must give the correct answer on every input.

cards.title: Does every unsatisfiable Boolean formula have a short efficiently checkable certificate?
cards.target: Do there exist a deterministic polynomial-time verifier V and a fixed polynomial p such that, for every Boolean CNF formula F, $F\text{ is unsatisfiable}\iff\exists\pi\in\{0,1\}^{\le p(|F|)}:V(F,\pi)=1$, with V never accepting a certificate for a satisfiable formula? Equivalently, is NP=coNP? The verification algorithm and polynomial are fixed for all formulas.

cards.title: Can randomness always be removed from polynomial-time decision algorithms?
cards.target: Does P=BPP? Precisely, for every language L for which a randomized Turing machine R runs in polynomial time on every input and every random tape, and satisfies $\Pr[R(x)=1_L(x)]\ge2/3$ for every binary string x, does there exist a deterministic polynomial-time Turing machine deciding L correctly on every x? The polynomial time bound of the deterministic machine may depend on R.
cards.scope: Quick screen of saved card fields; not a fresh full literature review.

cards.title: Can directed reachability be decided in deterministic logarithmic space?
cards.target: Is there a deterministic Turing machine A and an absolute constant C such that, for every directed graph G on vertices {1,...,n} and every s,t, A decides whether t is reachable from s while using at most $C\log_2(n+2)$ work-tape cells? G is supplied explicitly as a read-only adjacency matrix, together with s and t. The machine must halt and be correct on every input. This is equivalent to L=NL.

cards.title: Do single-pair shortest paths require cubic-size min-plus circuits?
cards.target: For n >= 2, assign an arbitrary nonnegative real weight x_{ij} to every unordered edge {i,j} of the complete undirected graph on vertices 1,...,n. cards.title: Hill’s conjecture for the crossing number of complete graphs
cards.target: For every integer n≥3, is the minimum number of edge crossings in a drawing of the complete graph K_n in the plane exactly $H(n)=\frac14\prod_{i=0}^{3}\left\lfloor\frac{n-i}{2}\right\rfloor$? Edges may be arbitrary simple curves. Drawings with H(n) crossings are known for every n; the unresolved assertion is that no drawing has fewer.

cards.title: Bipartite Exact Matching: deterministic polynomial time
cards.target: Given a bipartite graph $G=(L\cup R,E)$ with $|L|=|R|=n$, a red/blue coloring of its edges, and $k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}$, decide whether $G$ has a perfect matching containing exactly $k$ red edges. The historical question asks for a deterministic algorithm polynomial in the ordinary bit encoding of $(G,k)$. An April 2026 preprint claims such an algorithm. This entry records that claimed resolution and its verification limits; it is no longer labeled as a confirmed open problem.

cards.title: Can reachability diameter be approximated within a constant in near-linear time?
cards.target: For an unweighted directed graph $G=(V,E)$, define $D(G)=\max\{d_G(u,v):d_G(u,v)<\infty\}$. Is there an absolute constant $C\ge1$ and one randomized word-RAM algorithm that, on every input, returns an estimate $D(G)/C\le\widehat D\le D(G)$ with probability at least 2/3 in $\widetilde O(n+m)$ worst-case time? Here $n=|V|$, $m=|E|$, words have $\Theta(\log n)$ bits, and self-distances are included, giving D(G)=0 on an edgeless graph. The constant and the hidden logarithmic exponent are independent of G.

cards.title: How many rounds does triangle detection require in CONGEST?
cards.target: For arbitrary simple undirected n-vertex networks, determine the optimal worst-case randomized round complexity of triangle detection in CONGEST, up to constant factors. Each vertex initially knows its distinct O(log n)-bit identifier and its neighbors, and may send a separate O(log n)-bit message in each direction of every incident edge per synchronous round. On a triangle-free graph all vertices must output NO; otherwise at least one must output YES. The joint answer must be correct with probability at least 2/3 on every input and identifier assignment. The algorithm is uniform, has private random bits, and may know n. The currently established bounds are $\Omega(\log\log n)$ and $\widetilde O(n^{1/3})$.

cards.title: Information-theoretic classical verification of quantum computation
cards.target: Does there exist a uniform interactive protocol (P,V) for the following promise problem? Input is an explicit quantum circuit C over {H,T,CNOT}, starting on all-zero qubits, with one designated output bit and binary description length N. Let p(C) be the probability of output 1. YES instances have p(C)≥2/3 and NO instances have p(C)≤1/3. V is a classical probabilistic polynomial-time algorithm and the honest P is a quantum polynomial-time algorithm; they exchange only classical messages. On every YES instance, Pr[V accepts after interacting with P]≥2/3. On every NO instance, for every computationally unbounded cheating prover P*, Pr[V accepts after interacting with P*]≤1/3. Both honest running times, the number of rounds and total communication must be polynomial in N.
